content.title: Mark Pope is the oldest coach UK Basketball has ever hired | A Sea Of Blue
content.text: Skip to main contentSB NationSB Nation logoSign UpLoginA Kentucky Wildcats CommunityA Sea Of BlueMarch 26, 2026A Sea Of BlueNotificationsNotificationsNavigation DrawerLogin / Sign UpcloseCloseSearchFacebookTwitterYoutubeRSSKentucky Wildcats BasketballMark Pope is the oldest coach Kentucky has ever hiredPope’s first year as a coach was the same year John Calipari came to Kentucky.by Patrick CareyApr 12, 2024, 3:57 PM UTCFacebookLinkComments11Comment (All New)Mark Pope is officially the 23rd head basketball coach in Kentucky Basketball history after the announcement earlier this morning.Pope, 51 years old, is the oldest coach to be hired by Kentucky, passing John Calipari, who was 50 years old when he came to Lexington.UK statistician Corey Price posted on Twitter about the ages of each coach Kentucky has hired. Kentucky men’s basketball head coaches’ age at the time of their official hiring at the school:- 51 years, 7 months, 1 day (Mark Pope)- 50 years, 1 month, 22 days (John Calipari)- 49 years, 20 days (Eddie Sutton)- 47 years, 4 months, 30 days (Billy Gillispie)- 45 years,…— Corey Price (@coreyp08) April 12, 2024 Is it concerning that Pope is already 51 years old with a small coaching resume? Not really.Before Big Blue Nation freaks out, Pope played in the NBA until 2005, which pushed his coaching career back, so that chapter of his life got off to a late start.In fact, by the time Pope’s playing career ended, Scott Drew was already into his third as the head coach of Baylor.Pope’s first coaching job didn’t come until 2009 with the Georgia Bulldogs, which ironically was Calipari’s first year at Kentucky. So Pope’s overall coaching career began when Calipari’s Kentucky career began, so this is a bit of a full circle moment.This upcoming season will only be Pope’s 10th year as a head coach and just his
